title: Split and play
one: Shelf's bookmark cut twice: the halves make a pause, and the left tail a play.
idea: Shelf's bookmark cut twice, both cuts the same width, with nothing stamped on: C's slot down the middle makes the two halves a pause, and the second cut carries the notch's right edge straight on to the left side, so the left tail under it becomes a play pointing into the gap. The play's edges keep the notch's angle, so it has the shape of A's and B's play, and the outline is still the bookmark's.
built: The shared bookmark (candidates/base: 43.5 dp wide, top at 27.1, reach 32.56 of 33) with C's slot, 6.21 dp (1/7 of the width), and C's right half path for path: the build takes both from C's build, so a change to C's master carries into D. The second cut follows the notch's right edge carried on, from the right tip through the apex (which now falls inside the slot) to the left edge at y 52.69, two notches above the tips. The left half's upper piece ends on that line, so its lower edge and the right half's foot are one straight line, broken only by the slot. The cut lies under the line, 6.21 dp wide measured square to it (7.4 dp down the left edge): exactly the slot's width. The play is the tail under the cut. Its top edge runs parallel to the right flank and its bottom edge is the notch's own left flank, so the two edges mirror each other about a level axis and its depth is its height × 17/22, the shape of A's and B's play: 20.75 × 16.03 dp, 0.74 of A's 28.15 × 21.75, with its axis at y 70.46. Its rounded tip stops 4.23 dp short of the slot's line, 2.8 px on a 1× home screen, where the three pixel columns before the slot are clear (the nearest holds 4% paper). Between the pieces there is 6.21 dp of dark from the upper piece to the play and 10.7 dp from the play to the right half. I chose the cut's width by eye from 0.75, 1, 1.15 and 1.3 times the slot. At 0.75 the diagonal read as a crack beside the slot and the play's tip crowded the slot's line; at 1.15 and 1.3 the diagonal looked heavier than the slot and the play shrank away from the gap; at one slot the two read as cuts made with the same blade. A thinner cut gives a bigger play (22.6 dp tall at 0.75), but one slot is also the narrowest cut that keeps three clear pixel columns before the slot at 1×: at 0.95 of the slot the nearest column is 22% paper. The ink is 31.2% of the visible tile (C 34, base 38.9), and its centroid (55.1, 50.19) sits 1.1 dp right of the centre line, because the slot takes paper from both halves alike and the second cut from the left half only; the outline stays where every option's does. A corner's radius follows what made it, as in C. The outline makes the two square shoulders, which keep 4/34 of the width (5.12 dp). The cuts make every other corner, and all of them take the tips' 1.5/34 (1.92 dp): the two tail tips; the slot's four corners (right angles at the top, 57 degrees where the slot meets the diagonal and 123 where it meets the right half's foot); the diagonal's other corner on the upper piece, 123 degrees at the left edge; and the play's three corners, 57 degrees at the back and 66 at the point, its lower back corner being the bookmark's own left tip. That is nine corners at 1.92 dp and two at 5.12. In the pixel cuts every cut corner is sharp, as the base draws its tips.

small: The 48 and 32 px cuts keep both cuts and the play; the 16 px cut is C's split alone, and the glyph is the plain bookmark, as C's is. 48 px: C's 28 × 34 px bookmark, 4 px slot (1/7) and right half. The diagonal meets the left edge on whole pixels, at y 23 and, 6 px lower, at y 29, which makes it 5 px wide square to itself, a pixel wider than the slot. At the slot's own width (a 5 px drop) only two pixel columns stayed clear between the play's tip and the slot; the 6 px drop clears three (the nearest holds 4% paper; the sharp tip is 2.67 px short of the slot). Play 12 × 9.33 px, its axis on y 35, a pixel boundary, so its two edges rasterise as mirror images; 6.1% soft against C's 3.3. 32 px: C's 21 × 24 px bookmark (one pixel added on the left, so it sits half a pixel left of the tile's centre, as C's does) and 3 px slot. The notch's slope changes from C's 0.65 to 2/3, h1's at this size: on 0.65 the diagonal would meet the left edge at y 14.35 and its stairs start unevenly, while on 2/3 every end lands on a whole pixel, (5, 14), (14, 20), (17, 22) and (26, 28), and the stairs step evenly, three across and two down. The right half's foot ends 0.15 px higher at the slot than C's. A 4 px drop makes the diagonal 3.33 px wide, the slot's width to a third of a pixel. Play 10 × 7.5 px, axis on y 23; two clear pixel columns before the slot (the nearest holds 8% paper, under the sheet's 12% threshold; the sharp tip is 1.5 px short); 7.9% soft against C's 5.7. 16 px: C's cut, byte for byte apart from its comment, a 9 × 12 px bookmark half a pixel left of centre, with a 1 px slot and 45 degree stairs (2.4% soft, as C). A whole-pixel play fits (columns of 6, 4 and 2 px under a 2 px stair, its tip a pixel short of the slot), and magnified it is a play; at real size the stair and the slot join into one bent dark line, the left half breaks into two small pieces and the play reads as a nick in the left bar. The split alone keeps the outline whole but for the slot, and it is plainly the same icon. Glyph: the plain shared bookmark (6.3% soft, as C). Drawn as D it is a play-and-pause sign beside the clock, and on the media card it repeats the real button in both states, pause while playing and play while paused; at 24 px its play is also small, 7 × 5.6 px. media-card.png in this folder shows both (rebuild it with media-card.mjs).
risks: A play with a pause is the media toggle. A play and a pause cut from one shape can read as a player's play/pause button, or as a music or podcast app, before a reading app, and this is strongest in the light colourway, where three ink pieces stand on paper. The play sits in the bookmark's tail, under the left bar, and the outline keeps Shelf's square shoulders; both set it apart from the toggle sign. t2, a play beside a pause on a bookmark lying on its side, was dropped for reading as a remote. The old slash: the left half's lower edge and the right half's foot are one straight line from the left edge down to the right tip, top left to bottom right, the direction of the 'off' slash (bookmark-off, bell-off) that sank h1. Here the slot breaks it in the middle and the dark band crosses only the left half, so it reads as two bars cut at the notch's angle, but someone who knows the convention could still see a bookmark struck through. Lookalikes: Google Play Books pairs a bookmark and a play; the light colourway's two ink bars are still near ElevenLabs' II, though the left one is broken; any stock play/pause button. Like C, the notch's apex is gone, and the V survives as the play's lower edge and the right half's foot. The play is small: 20.75 dp tall against A's 28.15, about 13.8 × 10.7 px on a 1× home screen. The mark is three pieces of paper, so any one-colour use (print, emboss, a cut sticker) has to keep both cuts open. At 48 px the diagonal is a pixel wider than the slot (5 px against 4); at 32 px D's notch is 2/3 where C's is 0.65, so D's right half there is not C's file exactly; at 16 px and in the glyph D is C, so the play appears only from 32 px up. As the extension's toolbar button, which only saves, a play and a pause promise controls the extension doesn't have; the base's plain bookmark is the safer button there.
